metrics.summary: Indicates how the contact was terminated. This data is available in the Connect Customer contact record stream and Contact details page.
metrics.description:
Indicates how the contact was terminated. This data is available in the Connect Customer contact record stream and **Contact details** page.

The disconnect reason standardizes responses across different telephony providers into unified disconnect reasons. This helps you identify issues such as invalid numbers, call rejections, and spam blocking (both temporary and permanent). With these definitive telephony events, you can make data-driven decisions about how to handle call terminations.

Voice contacts can have the following disconnect reasons:

+ `TELECOM_BUSY` – The call attempt to the third party returns a network busy signal. This indicates the endpoint you are trying to call currently cannot take a call because it is currently engaged.

+ `TELECOM_NUMBER_INVALID` – The number you are attempting to call either lacks proper E164 formatting, or the number you are attempting to call does not exist or is no longer in use.

+ `TELECOM_POTENTIAL_BLOCKING` – The call attempt to the customer receives a response from multiple networks that suggest the number currently faces blocking based on network level blocks.

BlockReason – If the call is formally blocked using the 603\+ "Network Blocked", the [ FCC-mandated standard](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-25-15A1.pdf) that provides a uniform informative message that you can process and seek correction with the end customers carrier if you believe the traffic is blocked for invalid reasons, see [Segment attributes](connect-attrib-list.md#attribs-segment-attributes) for detail.

extraSections.Valid values:
+  `INBOUND`: The customer initiated voice (phone) contact with your contact center.
+  `OUTBOUND`: An agent initiated voice (phone) contact with the customer, by using the CCP to call their number.
+  `TRANSFER`: The customer was transferred by an agent to another agent or to a queue, using quick connects in the CCP. This results in the creation of a new contact record.
+  `CALLBACK`: The customer was contacted as part of a callback flow.
  For more information about the InitiationMethod in this scenario, see [Queued callbacks in real-time metrics in Connect Customer](about-queued-callbacks.md).
+  `API`: The contact was initiated with Connect Customer by API. This could be an outbound contact you created and queued to an agent, using the [StartOutboundVoiceContact](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_StartOutboundVoiceContact.html) API, or it could be a live chat that was initiated by the customer with your contact center, where you called the [StartChatConnect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_StartChatContact.html) API.
+  `WEBRTC_API`: The contact used the communication widget with video call.
+  `QUEUE_TRANSFER`: While the customer was in one queue (listening to Customer queue flow), they were transferred into another queue using a flow block.
+  `EXTERNAL_OUTBOUND`: An agent initiated voice (phone) contact with an external participant to your contact center using either quick connect in the CCP or a flow block.
+  `MONITOR`: A supervisor initiated monitor on an agent. The supervisor can silently monitor the agent and customer, or barge the conversation.
+  `DISCONNECT`: When a [Set disconnect flow](set-disconnect-flow.md) block is triggered, it specifies which flow to run after a disconnect event during a contact.
  A disconnect event is when:
  + A voice call ends when the customer hangs up, the agent hangs up, or the call drops because of a telecom or network issue.
  + A chat, or task is disconnected.
  + A task is disconnected as a result of a flow action.
  + A task expires. The task is automatically disconnected when it completes its expiry timer. The default is 7 days and task expiry is configurable up to 90 days.
  If a new contact is created while running a disconnect flow, then the initiation method for that new contact is DISCONNECT.
+  `AGENT_REPLY`: An agent has replied to an inbound email contact to create an outbound email reply.
+  `FLOW`: An email intiated by the [Send message](send-message.md) block.
+  `CAMPAIGN_PREVIEW`: The contact was initiated by an outbound campaign using preview dialing mode. The agent previews customer information before the call is placed.

metrics.name: ContactTraceRecord.InitiationTimestamp
metrics.summary: The date and time this contact was initiated, in UTC time.
metrics.description:
The date and time this contact was initiated, in UTC time.

+ For `INBOUND`, this is when the contact arrived.

+ For `OUTBOUND`, this is when the agent began dialing.

+ For `CALLBACK`, this is when the callback contact was created.

+ For `EXTERNAL_OUTBOUND`, this is when the agent started dialing the external participant.

+  For `MONITOR`, this is when the manager started listening to a contact.

+ For `TRANSFER` and `QUEUE_TRANSFER`, this is when the transfer was initiated.

In the case of tasks, InitiationTimestamp signifies when the task contact was created, whereas EnqueueTimestamp signifies time when the task contact was put in a queue to match the contact with agent.

You can configure flows so there is processing done on the task before a contact is queued. For example, this processing can take one minute or maybe several days. Many tasks, especially those used for backoffice processing aren't queued so they might have an InitiationTimestamp but not an EnqueueTimestamp.

Scheduled tasks get initiated when a contact is created, however they only start running flows when the schedule is met.

The 7 days expiry value is not absolute and there could be cases where tasks expire just beyond 7 days ( 7.01 days )

When [Transfer to phone number](transfer-to-phone-number.md) block is used without specifying a custom caller ID, the caller ID of the caller is passed as the caller ID. metrics.summary: ### Creating Custom Metric from Primitives
metrics.description: ### Creating Custom Metric from Primitives

extraSections.Each metric primitive can use the same m: Each metric primitive can only use a specific filter attribute once. If you apply the same filter attribute again (even with a different value), it will overwrite your previous condition.
extraSections.Metric primitives must be from the same:
Metric primitives are organized into categories based on what they measure (for example, Contact metrics, Agent metrics, Queue metrics). You can only combine primitives within the same category in a single custom metric. When selecting a metric primitive, you'll see its category in the dropdown. If a metric appears disabled (grayed out), pause on it to see the why, it must be from a different category than your first selection.

extraSections.Arithmetic operations on metric primitiv:
When performing arithmetic operations (\+, -, \*, /) on multiple metric primitives within a single statistic, all primitives must use the same filter attribute.

Important: The filter values can differ; only the filter attribute must match. 

Example: if the custom metric definition is of the form, SUM(Metric-1 \+ Metric-2), here the Metric-1 and Metric-2 must use consistent filters
extraSections.Arithmetic operations on statistics oper:
When performing arithmetic operations (\+, -, \*, /) on multiple statistics operations, you can combine metric primitive groups having different filters.

Example: 
+ Metric-1: a metric primitive from Contact category using Queue Time as a filter
+ Metric-2: a metric primitive from Contact category using Contact Handle Time as a filter
+ Valid custom metric definition: SUM(Metric-1) \+ SUM(Metric-2)
extraSections.Metrics only support specific statistics:
Not every metric primitive supports all statistic operations (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX). Using an unsupported statistic will cause an error.

Some metrics are only meaningful with certain calculations:
+ **Count-based metrics** (for example, Contacts Created): supports SUM, as AVG does not make sense
+ **Duration metrics** (for example, Contact Handle Time): support AVG, SUM, MIN, MAX
extraSections.A custom metric must have 1 to 5 compone:
A component is each individual metric primitive you add to your custom metric definition. If you're combining three different metrics, that's three components.
+ **Minimum**: 1 component (you must have at least one metric)
+ **Maximum**: 5 components per custom metric
extraSections.A statistic operation can support at mos: Each statistic operation (SUM, AVG) can contain a maximum of 10 elements.
extraSections.What Counts as an Element?: Both of these count toward the 10-element limit: + **Component identifiers** (for example, Metric\_1, Metric\_2) + **Constants/numbers** (for example, 100, 0.5) ### Guidelines for using custom metrics with out-of-the-box metrics A custom metric can only be added to a dashboard widget if the metric's underlying primitives support ALL filters and groupings applied to that widget. Common Scenario: You create a custom metric using "Agent Idle Time" primitive, which does NOT support "Channel" as a filter or grouping dimension. Result: You cannot add this custom metric to any widget that: + Filters by Channel, OR + Groups data by Channel Refer to the Metric Primitive definition section for supported filters and groupings of metric primitives.

metrics.notes: A custom metric using a metric primitive of **Current Contact** or **Current Agent** category can support at most 1 component.

metrics.name: Abandonment rate
metrics.summary: This metric measures the percentage of abandoned contacts. An abandoned contact refers to a contact that was disconnected by the customer while in queue. This means that they weren't connected to an agent. Contacts queued for callback are not counted as abandoned.
metrics.description:
This metric measures the percentage of abandoned contacts. An abandoned contact refers to a contact that was disconnected by the customer while in queue. This means that they weren't connected to an agent. Contacts queued for callback are not counted as abandoned.

The abandonment rate helps you identify potential issues with long wait times or inefficient queue management. A high abandonment rate might indicate a need for additional staffing, improved call routing strategies, or addressing queue bottlenecks.
metrics.calculationLogic: + (Contacts abandoned / Contacts queues ) \* 100.0
metrics.notes: When using the **Routing Profile** grouping, the abandonment rate shows as 0. This is because abandoned calls occur when customers disconnect before being connected to an agent, so there is no routing profile association. A routing profile is only assigned when an agent accepts a contact.

metrics.name: Active slots
metrics.summary: This metric counts the number of active contact handling slots across all agents.
metrics.description:
This metric counts the number of active contact handling slots across all agents.

A slot is considered active when it contains a contact that is:
+ Connected
+ On Hold
+ In After Contact Work
+ Paused
+ In Outbound ring state

This metric helps organizations:
+ Monitor concurrent contact handling capacity.
+ Track real-time channel use.
+ Plan capacity management.

metrics.name: Adherence
metrics.summary: This metric is available in AWS Regions only where Forecasting & agent scheduling is available.
metrics.description:
This metric is available in AWS Regions only where [Forecasting & agent scheduling](regions.md#optimization_region) is available.

This metric measures the percentage of time that an agent correctly follows their schedule. 

Adherence is calculated as Adherent time divided by the sum of Adherent time and Non-adherent time. Scheduled time is not used in this calculation.

When adherence thresholds are configured, time that an agent is adherent outside their scheduled shift counts toward Adherent time. As a result, Adherent time plus Non-adherent time can be greater than Scheduled time. The Adherence percentage cannot be derived from Scheduled time.
metrics.notes:
+ Any time you change the schedule, Schedule Adherence is re-calculated up to 30 days in the past from the current date (not the date of the schedule), if schedules are changed.

For a list of all schedule adherence metrics, see [Schedule Adherence metrics in Connect Customer](scheduling-metrics.md).

metrics.name: Agent Activity

metrics.description:
This column heading appears on Real-time metrics reports. It's not a metric exactly, but a indicator of the agent's activity state.

If an agent is handling a single contact, this metric might have the following values: Available, Incoming, On contact, Rejected, Missed, Error, After contact work, or a custom status. 

If an agent is handling concurrent contacts, Connect Customer uses the following logic to determine the state: 
+ If at least one contact is in Error, Agent Activity = **Error**.
+ Else if at least one contact is Missed contact, Agent Activity = **Missed**.
+ Else if at least one contact is Rejected contact, Agent Activity = **Rejected**.
+ Else if at least one contact is Connected, On Hold, Paused, or Outbound contact/Outbound callback, Agent Activity = **On contact**.
+ Else if at least one contact is After contact work, Agent Activity = **After Contact Work**.
+ Else if at least one contact is Incoming/Inbound Callback, Agent Activity = **Incoming**.
+ Else if agent status is a custom status, Agent Activity is the custom status.
+ Else if agent status is Available, Agent Activity = **Available**.
+ Else if agent status is Offline, Agent Activity = **Offline**. (After an agent moves to Offline, they disappear from the real-time metrics page in 5-10 minutes.)

If a manager is using the Manager Monitor feature to monitor a particular agent as they interact with a customer, then the manager's Agent Activity will display as Monitoring. The Agent Activity of the agent who is being monitored is still On Contact.

metrics.name: Availability
metrics.summary: This metric shows the current number of slots that are available for each agent for routing new contacts. A slot is considered available when: + The agent is in Available status + The slot is not currently handling a contact + The agent's routing profile allows for that channel + The agent is not at their concurrent contact limit
metrics.description:
This metric shows the current number of slots that are available for each agent for routing new contacts. A slot is considered available when:
+ The agent is in Available status
+ The slot is not currently handling a contact
+ The agent's routing profile allows for that channel
+ The agent is not at their concurrent contact limit

A slot becomes unavailable when it contains a contact that is:
+ Connected
+ In ACW
+ Inbound/outbound ringing
+ Missed
+ In error state
+ On hold
+ Agent is in a custom status
+ Agent can't take contacts from that channel per routing profile

The number of available slots for an agent are based on their [routing profile](routing-profiles.md). For example, let's say an agent's routing profile specifies they can handle either one voice contact **or** up to three chat contacts simultaneously. If they are currently handling one chat, they have two available slots left, not three.

What causes this number to go down? A slot is considered unavailable when:
+ A contact in the slot is: connected to the agent, in After Contact Work, inbound ringing, outbound ringing, missed, or in an error state.
+ A contact in the slot is connected to the agent and on hold.

Connect Customer doesn't count an agent's slots when:
+ The agent has set their status in the CCP to a custom status, such as Break or Training. Connect Customer doesn't count these slots because agents can't take inbound contacts when they've set their status to a custom status. 
+ The agent can't take contacts from that channel per their routing profile.

This metric measures the number of agents who can take an inbound contact. An agent can only take inbound contacts when they manually set their status to Available in the CCP (or in some cases when their manager changes it).

This is different from how many more inbound contacts an agent could take. If you want to know how many more contacts an agent can have routed to them, look at the Availability metric. It indicates how many slots the agent has free.

What causes this number to go down? An agent is considered **unavailable** when: 
+ The agent has set their status in the CCP to a custom status, such as Break or Training. Connect Customer doesn't count these slots because agents can't take inbound contacts when they've set their status to a custom status. 
+ The agent has at least one contact ongoing. 
+ The agent has a contact in a missed or error state, which prevents the agent from taking any more contacts until they are flipped back to routable.

metrics.calculationLogic:

  + If NextContactId is present, then skip this record.
  + If (PreDisconnectState is present AND PreDisconnectState == "IN\_QUEUE" AND TransferCompletedTimestamp is present), then skip this record.
  + If QueueInfo.Duration is less than the value of X, then count this record as 1.
+ Return final\_result = sum of the counts across all contacts.

It tracks the number of inbound and outbound contacts across all channels (voice, chat, task) that were generated during the specified time period. It can be filtered by initiation methods. 

This metric is useful for understanding the overall contact volume and workload within the contact center.
metrics.calculationLogic:
+ The calculation definition returns a value of 1 for each contact record processed, effectively counting the number of contact records present within the specified time range.
+ For each contact record processed during the specified time period, the calculation returns a value of 1.
+ The metric aggregates these individual values of 1 using the SUM calculation statistic, resulting in the total count of contacts created within the time range.

metrics.name: Contacts handled
metrics.summary: This metric counts the contacts that were connected to an agent during a given time period. It doesn't matter how the contact got to the agent. It could be a customer calling your contact center, or an agent calling the customer. It could be a contact transferred from one agent to another. It could be a contact where the agent answered it, but then they weren't sure what to do and they transferred the contact away again. As long as the agent was connected to the contact, it increments Contacts handled.
metrics.description:

It could be a customer calling your contact center, or an agent calling the customer. It could be a contact transferred from one agent to another. It could be a contact where the agent answered it, but then they weren't sure what to do and they transferred the contact away again. As long as the agent was connected to the contact, it increments **Contacts handled**. 

This metric provides a measure of the workload handled by agents. You can use it to understand agent use and capacity planning. Contacts handled is particularly useful for contact centers that need to track the volume of customer interactions handled by their agents.

metrics.name: Contacts resolved in X seconds
metrics.summary: This metric provides the count of contacts that have a resolution duration between 0 and X seconds after being initiated based on InitiationTimestamp. The resolution time for a contact is defined as: beginning from InitiationTimestamp, and ending at AfterContactWorkEndTimestamp or DisconnectTimestamp, whichever one is later.
metrics.description:
This metric provides the count of contacts that have a resolution duration between 0 and X seconds after being initiated based on `InitiationTimestamp`. The resolution time for a contact is defined as: beginning from [InitiationTimestamp](ctr-data-model.md#initiationtimestamp), and ending at [AfterContactWorkEndTimestamp](ctr-data-model.md#acwendtimestamp) or [DisconnectTimestamp](ctr-data-model.md#disconnecttimestamp), whichever one is later. 

You can create custom duration to get this metric. Choose from additional durations, such as minutes, hours, or days. The maximum duration for a custom value is 7 days. That's because in Connect Customer you can't have a contact that lasts longer than 7 days.

This metric helps measure the efficiency of your contact center in resolving customer inquiries within a specified time threshold.
metrics.calculationLogic:
+ For each contact record
  + If InitiationTimestamp is NOT present, then skip this record.
  + If Agent.AfterContactWorkEndTimestamp is present AND Agent.AfterContactWorkEndTimestamp is greater than DisconnectTimestamp, then: 
    + set end\_time = Agent.AfterContactWorkEndTimestamp.
  + Else, set end\_time = DisconnectTimestamp.
  + set diff\_value = end\_time - InitiationTimestamp. 
  + If diff\_value is greater than 0, then set result = diff\_value.
  + Else, set result = 0.
+ Return final\_result = sum of the counts across all contact records.

metrics.name: Flows outcome

metrics.description:
This metric returns the count for following flow outcomes within the specified start time and end time. The outcomes are terminal blocks in a flow.

 For a given start and end time this metric shows the count those flows where the start time is between the start and end interval specified and has end time. The end time of flow can be greater than end time specified in query interval. The metric does not show the count of flow that started before the start time and is in progress during the specified interval
metrics.calculationLogic:
+ Check flow\_endTimestamp present?
+ Return Count = 1 if end timestamp is present, else return 0.
metrics.notes:
+ Uses SUM statistic for aggregation.
+ Counts completed flows with defined outcomes.
+ Only counts flows that started within specified time range.
+ Data for this metric is available starting from April 22, 2024 0:00:00 GMT.
+ System-defined flow outcomes include: 
  + **DROPPED**: When a contact drops from the flow before reaching terminal block.
  + **DISCONNECTED\_PARTICIPANT**: When a contact reaches a [Disconnect / hang up](disconnect-hang-up.md) terminal block in a flow.
  + **ENDED\_FLOW\_EXECUTION**: When a contact reaches an [End flow / Resume](end-flow-resume.md) terminal block in a flow.
  + **TRANSFERED\_TO\_AGENT**: When a contact is transferred to an agent after running a [Transfer to agent (beta)](transfer-to-agent-block.md) block. 
  + **TRANSFERED\_TO\_PHONE\_NUMBER**: When a contact is transferred to a phone number specified in a [Transfer to phone number](transfer-to-phone-number.md) block. 
  + **TRANSFERED\_TO\_FLOW**: When a contact is transferred to another flow specified in a [Transfer to flow](transfer-to-flow.md) block.

This metric provides the percentage of contacts removed from the queue between 0 and *X* after being added to it. A contact is removed from a queue when the following occurs: an agent answers the contact, the customer abandons the contact, or the customer requests a call back. 

For *X* you can choose from pre-set times in seconds: 15, 20, 25, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, and 600.
metrics.calculationLogic: + This percentage is calculated as follows: (Contacts removed from queue in *X* seconds / Contacts queued) \* 100 ### Custom service levels You can also create custom service level metrics. Choose from additional durations, such as minutes, hours, or days. Custom service levels are localized to the report where they are created. For example, you create a report that has a custom service level of 75. You leave the page and then create another report. The custom service level 75 won't exist in the second report. You'll need to create it again. The maximum duration for a custom service level is 7 days. That's because in Connect Customer you can't have a contact that goes longer than 7 days. metrics.name: Staffed agents

metrics.description:
This metric counts the total number of agents who are online, and not in NPT (a custom status). 

An agent is NOT counted when:
+ Their CCP status is set to **Offline**. 
+ Their CCP status is set to any custom status (Break, Training, Lunch, and more). 

An agent IS counted when:
+ They are in Available status (whether handling contacts or not) .
+ They are in Available status and making outbound calls.

Example scenarios:
+ Agent in Available status making outbound call: Staffed = 1
+ Agent in Break status making outbound call: Staffed = 0
+ Agent in Available status handling multiple contacts: Staffed = 1
+ Agent logged in but in Training status: Staffed = 0

This metric helps organizations:
+ Track actual operational staffing levels.
+ Monitor workforce adherence to schedules.
+ Calculate real-time staffing efficiency.
+ Compare scheduled vs actual staffing levels.
+ Support workforce management decisions.

extraSections.Related metrics:
+ AGENTS\_ONLINE (includes all online agents regardless of status)
+ AGENTS\_NON\_PRODUCTIVE (shows agents in custom statuses)
+ AGENTS\_AVAILABLE (shows agents ready for contact routing)
extraSections.Common use cases:
+ Workforce Management
  + Compare actual vs scheduled staffing
  + Monitor real-time adherence
  + Track staffing efficiency
+ Operations Management
  + Monitor operational capacity
  + Track agent availability patterns
  + Support intraday management decisions
+ Performance Analysis
  + Calculate staffing efficiency metrics
  + Analyze staffing patterns
  + Support capacity planning

metrics.notes:
+ The AGENTS\_STAFFED metric is crucial for workforce management and operations as it provides the clearest picture of actual operational capacity by counting only those agents who are truly available for work (not in custom statuses). It's often used in conjunction with other metrics to understand the full staffing situation and make informed decisions about resource allocation and management.
+ The key distinction between this and other metrics like AGENTS\_ONLINE is that it specifically excludes agents in custom statuses, providing a more accurate view of actual operational capacity.
+ For information about why this metric might appear incorrect in a report, see [Why your Login/Logout report might appear incorrect](login-logout-reports.md#login-logout-incorrect).

+ Grant other users permission to the Admin security profile. People assigned to the Admin security profile have full access to your contact center.
Doing these things would enable someone to lock out those who need to access Connect Customer, and allow in others who can steal customer data and damage your business.
You can limit this risk by adding [tag-based access control](tag-based-access-control.md) on the security profile. For example, you can apply tag-based access control to deny access to administrators and the Admin security profile. metrics.name: Capacity plan
metrics.summary: A plan that turns forecasts and a scenario into staffing targets for a date range.
metrics.description: A capacity plan helps you determine how many agents your contact center needs. It uses forecasts and scenario inputs to set staffing targets for a given time period. Open a plan to review its output, override values (Hiring plans only), re-run it after new forecasts are published, download it, or publish it to make it official.

metrics.name: Plan type
metrics.summary: Hiring plan (long-term FTE estimates) or Scheduling plan (interval-level headcount).
metrics.description:
+ **Hiring plan**: long-term FTE (full-time equivalent) estimates up to 64 weeks ahead, for hiring and workforce planning. Uses both a long-term and a short-term forecast; the two should overlap by at least 4 weeks (1 day minimum).
+ **Scheduling plan**: interval-level headcount needs in 15- or 30-minute intervals for scheduling and resource use. Needs only a published short-term forecast, and the plan dates must fall within that forecast's range.

metrics.name: Plan status
metrics.summary: Whether the plan has finished computing.
metrics.description: The state of the plan's computation. A plan is generated from the selected forecast group and scenario and shows **Complete** when its output is ready to review. Re-running the plan recomputes it from the latest published forecasts.

metrics.name: Plan start and end dates
metrics.summary: The period the plan covers.
metrics.description: The first and last dates covered by the plan. Hiring plans can extend up to 64 weeks ahead; Scheduling plan dates must fall within the published short-term forecast's date range, and its output is reviewed up to 7 days at a time.

metrics.name: Forecast group
metrics.summary: The forecast group whose published forecasts feed this plan.
metrics.description: The forecast group used as input. Hiring plans use its published long-term and short-term forecasts; Scheduling plans use its published short-term forecast. The forecasted contact volume and AHT in the output reflect only this forecast group, so consider re-running the plan after new forecasts are published.

metrics.name: Planning scenario
metrics.summary: The what-if assumptions a plan is generated with: occupancy, attrition, FTE hours, shrinkage, hours of operation, and per-channel targets.
metrics.description: A scenario has two parts. **Scenario inputs**: maximum occupancy, daily attrition (annual attrition divided by about 250 working days), FTE hours per week, optional outsourced contacts, maximum overtime and voluntary time off allowed, shrinkage, and the hours of operation your agents work. **Optimization inputs**: one target per channel, for up to four channels: service level (all channels), average speed of answer (Voice and Chat) or average time to complete (Task and Email, which treats the channel as asynchronous and uses backlog projections). You then generate a capacity plan from the scenario.

metrics.name: Associated capacity plans
metrics.summary: How many capacity plans were generated with this scenario.
metrics.description: The number of capacity plans that use this scenario. The same scenario can be used to generate several plans, for example best-case and worst-case assumptions against different forecast groups or date ranges.

metrics.name: Created
metrics.summary: When, and by whom, the item was created.
metrics.description: The creation date, and for scenarios the user who created it. Plans record the user who published them separately.

metrics.name: Last computed
metrics.summary: When the plan's output was last generated or re-run.
metrics.description: When the plan was last computed. Re-run a plan after new forecasts are published, or after changing the hours of operation used by its scenario, so the output reflects the latest inputs.

metrics.name: Last modified
metrics.summary: When the scenario's inputs were last edited.
metrics.description: When the scenario was last changed. Editing a scenario does not change plans already generated from it; re-run those plans to apply the new assumptions.

metrics.name: Published
metrics.summary: When, and by whom, the plan was published to make it official.
metrics.description: Publishing a capacity plan makes it the official plan you share with Human Resources, Finance and Training. The table shows the publish date and the user who published it.

metrics.name: Forecasted Contact Volume
metrics.summary: The total forecasted contact volume across the channels in the scenario's optimization targets.
metrics.description: The total forecasted contact volume across the channels in your selected scenario's optimization targets. It reflects only the selected forecast group; after new forecasts are published, re-run the plan to pick up the latest values.

metrics.name: Forecasted Average Handling Time (AHT), seconds
metrics.summary: The forecasted average handling time across the channels in the scenario's optimization targets.
metrics.description: The forecasted average handling time, in seconds, across the channels in your selected scenario's optimization targets. It reflects only the selected forecast group; after new forecasts are published, re-run the plan.

metrics.name: Required FTEs (without Shrinkage)
metrics.summary: How many full-time equivalent agents need to be hired to meet the business goals, ignoring shrinkage.
metrics.description: How many full-time equivalent agents need to be hired to meet the defined business goals (such as the service level target), without considering shrinkage.

metrics.name: Required FTEs (with Shrinkage)
metrics.summary: How many FTEs need to be hired to meet the business goals once shrinkage is accounted for.
metrics.description: How many full-time equivalent agents need to be hired to meet the defined business goals (such as the service level target), with shrinkage considered. Shrinkage comes from the scenario's total shrinkage percentage or from day-level values uploaded on the Import data tab.

metrics.name: Forecasted Occupancy %
metrics.summary: The occupancy agents are forecast to have under this plan.
metrics.description: How much occupancy is forecast for the agents: the share of their time spent handling contacts under the planned staffing. The scenario's maximum occupancy input caps it.

metrics.name: Available FTEs
metrics.summary: How many agents are available to work that period, from the data you import.
metrics.description: How many agents are available for working that day. It is uploaded in the **Import data** section; the gap, OT and VTO metrics are calculated from it.

metrics.name: Gap between available and required FTEs
metrics.summary: The difference between available FTEs and required FTEs, also shown as a percentage.
metrics.description: The difference between available FTEs and required FTEs, and **Gap %**, that difference as a percentage. A negative gap is a supply deficit, a positive gap a surplus.

uiLabels.label: Gap between available FTEs and required FTEs

metrics.name: Required OT %
metrics.summary: How much overtime would cover a supply deficit.
metrics.description: If there is a supply deficit (required FTEs higher than available FTEs), required OT % indicates how much overtime would be needed to cover the deficit. The scenario's maximum overtime allowed bounds it.

metrics.name: Required VTO %
metrics.summary: How much voluntary time off could absorb a supply surplus.
metrics.description: If there is a supply surplus (required FTEs lower than available FTEs), required VTO % indicates how much voluntary time off could be used to lower agent idle time and thus lower costs. The scenario's maximum VTO allowed bounds it.

metrics.name: Required headcount
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: how many agents are needed in this 15- or 30-minute interval.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the number of agents needed in each interval to meet the channel targets. The interval size matches your short-term forecast settings. The Headcount requirements graph plots the same series.

metrics.name: Available headcount
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: how many agents are available in this interval, from imported headcount data.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the agents available in each interval, taken from the interval-level headcount data you import for Scheduling plans.

metrics.name: Net staffing
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: available headcount minus required headcount for the interval.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the difference between available and required headcount in each interval, before shrinkage. Negative values show understaffed intervals.

metrics.name: Total shrinkage
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: the shrinkage applied to the interval.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the total shrinkage applied to each interval, from the scenario's shrinkage percentage or the interval-level shrinkage data you import.

metrics.name: Required headcount with shrinkage
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: required headcount once shrinkage is accounted for.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the agents needed in each interval after applying shrinkage.

metrics.name: Net staffing with shrinkage
metrics.summary: Scheduling plan: available headcount minus required headcount with shrinkage.
metrics.description: In a Scheduling plan, the difference between available headcount and required headcount with shrinkage, per interval.

metrics.name: Contact status
metrics.summary: Whether the contact is completed or still in progress.
metrics.description:
Whether the contact is completed or still in progress. You can search for both completed and in-progress contacts. For contacts handled by agents, a contact is only marked as completed after the agent has completed After Contact Work (ACW).

The ability to search for in-progress contacts varies by channel: queued callbacks appear once queued; other voice contacts only after they are connected to an agent or disconnected; chats after they are connected to the system, queued, connected to an agent or disconnected; tasks and email as soon as they are initiated.

metrics.name: Contact duration
metrics.summary: How long the contact lasted, as shown by the Contact search page.
metrics.description: How long the contact lasted, as shown by the Contact search page. This is not a field of the contact record itself; the record stores the contact's **InitiationTimestamp** and **DisconnectTimestamp**, and per-segment durations such as **AgentInteractionDuration**, **CustomerHoldDuration** and **AfterContactWorkDuration**.

metrics.name: First contact flow
metrics.summary: The flow that first handled the contact.
metrics.description: The flow that first handled the contact, shown by ID or by name. The Contact search page also lets you filter by the name of the initial flow for the contact.

metrics.name: Is transferred out
metrics.summary: Whether the contact was transferred out to another agent, queue, or an external number.
metrics.description: Indicates whether the contact was transferred out to another agent, queue, or an external number. This option only indicates cold transfers, where the agent disconnected before the contact was transferred. For the date and time (in UTC time) when the transfer was connected, see **TransferCompletedTimestamp** in the contact record.

metrics.name: Task template name
metrics.summary: The task template used to create a task contact.
metrics.description: The task template used to create a task contact. Filtering contacts by task template does not reflect updated templates for in-progress contacts: Contact search shows the original template until the contact terminates.

metrics.name: Forecast
metrics.summary: A forecast of future contact volume or average handle time for a forecast group, named after the group.
metrics.description: Forecasts are a projection of the workload in your contact center. Connect generates them per forecast group from historical metrics; they include inbound, transfer and callback contacts across voice, chat, task and email. Each forecast group gets one forecast per type you select, and each forecast covers one metric (contact volume or average handling time). You can inspect a forecast before publishing it, download it, override it, or delete it; deleting a forecast affects capacity plans and schedules built from it.

metrics.name: Forecast type
metrics.summary: Short-term (18 weeks, updated daily, for scheduling) or Long-term (64 weeks, updated weekly, for capacity planning).
metrics.description:
+ **Short-term** forecasts are automatically updated daily and are used for scheduling agents and interval-level headcount estimation, up to 18 weeks ahead.
+ **Long-term** forecasts are automatically updated every week, on the weekday the forecast was created, and are used for capacity planning up to 64 weeks ahead.

Intraday forecasts (updated every 15 minutes, for queues with at least 5000 unique contacts per week per queue-channel over the last 4 weeks) appear on the Intraday forecast performance dashboard rather than here. Only the most current forecast is kept, so download a day's forecast if you need to keep it.

metrics.name: Forecast metric
metrics.summary: What the forecast predicts: Contact Volume or Average Handling Time.
metrics.description: Each forecast predicts one metric for the forecast group: **Contact Volume** (the number of contacts expected per interval) or **Average Handling Time** (the expected average handle time). Both are produced for each forecast type you create, because capacity planning and scheduling need both.

metrics.name: Forecast status
metrics.summary: Scheduled while the forecast is being computed, Complete when it is ready.
metrics.description: When a forecast is created its status is **Scheduled**; it becomes **Complete** when the computation finishes. A first short-term or long-term forecast is typically available within 4 hours, often in about 1 hour. Changes to the forecast group (importing historical data, adding or removing queues) trigger a recomputation in the same timeframe.

metrics.name: Last computed
metrics.summary: When Connect last recalculated this forecast with the most current contact data.
metrics.description: The date the forecast was last computed. Short-term forecasts are recomputed daily and long-term forecasts weekly, always from the most current contact data; the models themselves are retrained weekly (short-term) and monthly (long-term). On the inspect page you can compare the **Last computed forecast** with the **Last published forecast**.

metrics.name: Last published
metrics.summary: When this forecast was last published for use by capacity planning and scheduling.
metrics.description: The date the forecast was last published. Publishing makes the forecast available to schedulers and to capacity planning; a published long-term forecast is required before a capacity plan can be created, and a published short-term forecast before a schedule can be generated. Inspect and, if needed, override a forecast before publishing it.

metrics.name: Forecast group
metrics.summary: A set of queues forecast together; each queue belongs to exactly one group.
metrics.description: Forecast groups combine different queues into one forecast, so the forecast is built from aggregated data across those queues. Group queues that share the same pool of agents, since forecast groups are associated with a staffing group for scheduling. Each queue can belong to only one forecast group, at least one group is needed before any forecast, and it is best to create all groups before creating forecasts so all relevant historical data trains the model.

metrics.name: Number of queues
metrics.summary: How many queues are in the forecast group.
metrics.description: The number of queues assigned to the forecast group. Adding or removing queues later can trigger an immediate recomputation of the associated forecasts and affects downstream capacity plans and schedules. A disabled queue can stay in the group: it simply stops contributing contacts over time.

metrics.name: Demand groups
metrics.summary: Subsets of a forecast group's queues that are forecast separately, for example per language.
metrics.description: Demand groups are distinct work subsets within a forecast group, each corresponding to specific queues that require specialised agent skills. They let one forecast group produce separate demand forecasts, for example per language, and scheduling then calculates headcount per demand group. A queue can be in only one demand group.

metrics.name: Date modified
metrics.summary: When the forecast group's queues or settings were last changed.
metrics.description: The date the forecast group was last changed. A change today, such as adding a queue, makes Connect compute new short-term and long-term forecasts for the group, and affects capacity plans and schedules based on it.

metrics.name: Quick connect name
metrics.summary: A unique name for the quick connect, shown to agents in the Contact Control Panel when they transfer a contact.
metrics.description:
Enter a unique name for the quick connect. Agents see this name in the Contact Control Panel (CCP) under **Quick connects**.

Quick connects are a way to create a list of destinations for common transfers. For example, you might create a quick connect for Tier 2 support: if agents in Tier 1 support can't solve the issue, they transfer the contact to Tier 2.

Agents only see the quick connects of the queues in their routing profile, including the Default outbound queue. To make a quick connect visible, add it to the queue on the **Edit queue** page.

metrics.name: Description
metrics.summary: Optional text describing what the quick connect is for.
metrics.description: Optional text describing what the quick connect is for. It is shown in the quick connects list and on the quick connect's detail page, and can be searched from the list page.

metrics.name: Type
metrics.summary: The kind of destination: Phone number, User, Queue, or Flow.
metrics.description:
The type of a quick connect specifies the destination:

+ **Phone number**: contacts are transferred to a phone number (such as an on-call pager). No flows are involved; the call is connected directly to the destination, so you cannot set the outbound caller ID and the caller ID from the queue configuration is used. These external quick connects appear in the CCP at all times.
+ **User**: contacts are transferred to a specific user, such as an agent, as part of a flow (the agent transfer flow you choose).
+ **Queue**: contacts are transferred to a queue as part of a flow (the queue transfer flow you choose).
+ **Flow**: agent-initiated contacts that provide interactive workflows during an active chat session. Flow quick connects are only supported for chat contacts.

**Important:** User and Queue quick connects only appear in the CCP when an agent goes to transfer a contact.

metrics.name: Destination
metrics.summary: Where contacts go when agents use this quick connect: a phone number, a user, a queue, or a flow, depending on the type.
metrics.description: Where contacts are sent when an agent uses this quick connect. Depending on the **Type**, this is a phone number (entered with its country code), the name of a user such as an agent, the name of a queue, or a flow. For User and Queue quick connects you also choose the transfer flow that runs when the quick connect is used.

metrics.name: Phone number
metrics.summary: For a Phone number quick connect: the destination number, starting with the country code.
metrics.description:
For a **Phone number** quick connect, enter the destination number starting with the country code. In the US, the country code is 1. For example, a supervisor's mobile phone so agents can call them if needed.

When an agent uses an external quick connect the call is connected directly to the destination without invoking any flows, and caller ID is taken from the queue configuration. The customer hears the Customer hold flow while the transfer is in progress.

metrics.name: Queue
metrics.summary: For a Queue quick connect: the queue contacts are transferred to, through the chosen queue transfer flow.
metrics.description: For a **Queue** quick connect, the queue that contacts are transferred to. When an agent chooses the quick connect, the queue transfer flow associated with it runs; that flow's **Transfer to queue** block places the contact in the queue, and an available agent working that queue is notified to accept it. Agent and customer whisper flows then play before the agents are connected.

metrics.name: User
metrics.summary: For a User quick connect: the user, such as an agent, that contacts are transferred to, through the chosen agent transfer flow.
metrics.description: For a **User** quick connect, the user (for example an agent) that contacts are transferred to. When an agent chooses the quick connect, the agent transfer flow associated with it runs and the destination agent is notified in their CCP to accept or reject the contact. The call is not connected until they accept; agent and customer whisper flows then play before the agents are connected.

metrics.name: Flow
metrics.summary: The flow run when this quick connect is used: a transfer flow for User and Queue types, or the agent-initiated flow for a Flow quick connect.
metrics.description: The flow run when this quick connect is used. For **User** quick connects this is an agent transfer flow; for **Queue** quick connects it is a queue transfer flow. For a **Flow** quick connect it is the agent-initiated flow that provides an interactive workflow during an active chat session (chat contacts only). Phone number quick connects involve no flow.

metrics.name: Tags
metrics.summary: Key/value tags used to identify, organize, search for, filter and control access to the quick connect.
metrics.description: Optional key/value tags that help you identify, organize, search for and filter quick connects, and control who can access them through tag-based access control in security profiles.

metrics.name: ARN
metrics.summary: The Amazon Resource Name that uniquely identifies this quick connect, used with the quick connect APIs.
metrics.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this quick connect. Use it, or the ID it ends with, when calling APIs such as DescribeQuickConnect, UpdateQuickConnectConfig or AssociateQueueQuickConnects.

metrics.name: Channel availability
metrics.summary: Choose which types of contacts will be routed to agents who are assigned to this routing profile.
metrics.description:
Choose which types of contacts (voice, chat, task, email) will be routed to agents who are assigned to this routing profile. The **Status** toggle enables or disables each channel for the whole profile.

For example, if 20 queues assigned to a profile are all enabled for voice, chat, task and email, removing the **Voice** option at the routing profile level stops all voice calls to these agents across all queues in the profile. Select **Voice** again to restart voice contacts for them.

The channels you enable here must match the channels chosen for each queue in the **Queues** section; otherwise contacts from that channel are not routed to agents.

metrics.name: Maximum contacts per agent
metrics.summary: For chat, task and email channels, how many contacts an agent can handle simultaneously, up to 10.
metrics.description:
For chat, task, and email channels, specify how many contacts an agent can handle simultaneously, up to 10.

For emails, this field defines how many emails agents can receive, and double that number is how many outbound emails agents can initiate. For example, if you set **Maximum contacts per agent** to 5, agents can receive up to 5 emails and create up to 10 agent-initiated outbound emails.

When workload type concurrency is enabled for a channel, this field is disabled for that channel and capacity is configured per workload type row instead.

metrics.name: Cross-channel concurrency
metrics.summary: Whether agents can be offered contacts from other channels while already handling this channel.
metrics.description:
Choose one of the following options:

+ **No other channels while agent is on `channel`**. For example, while an agent is on a chat, they will not receive a voice contact, email, or a task.
+ **Allow other channels concurrently**. For example, while an agent is on a voice contact, they can be offered contacts from any other channels enabled in the routing profile, such as chats, emails, and tasks.

When using cross-channel concurrency, Connect checks which contact to offer the agent as follows: it checks what contacts/channels the agent is currently handling; based on that and the cross-channel configuration in the agent's routing profile, it determines whether the agent can be routed the next contact; and it prioritizes the longest waiting contact if Priority and Delay are equal, so First-In First-Out is still respected across channels.

When workload type concurrency is enabled for a channel, this field becomes inactive for that channel and cross-channel behaviour is set per workload type.

metrics.name: Workload type concurrency
metrics.summary: (Task and Email channels only) Configure agent capacity per workload type instead of a single channel-level number.
metrics.description:
(Task and Email channels only) Toggle this on to configure agent capacity per workload type instead of a single channel-level number. When enabled, the **Maximum contacts per agent** field is disabled for that channel, and you configure capacity through individual workload type rows instead.

Workload type values come from the system predefined attribute `connect:WorkloadType`; you must create them before they appear here. If a contact's workload type doesn't match any entry in the routing profile, the contact stays in queue.

metrics.name: Workload type rows
metrics.summary: Add one row per workload type the agent should handle on this channel, with its concurrency and cross-channel behaviour.
metrics.description:
Under the channel, choose **Add workload type** and configure each row:

+ **Workload Type**: a value of the system predefined attribute `connect:WorkloadType`.
+ **Concurrency**: the number of contacts of this workload type the agent can handle simultaneously (1 to 10).
+ **Cross-channel behavior**: **No other channels or workload types**, **Only allow other workload types of the same channel**, or **Allow other channels concurrently**.

Rules: up to 5 workload types per channel in a single routing profile; the sum of concurrency values across a channel's workload types cannot exceed the channel's maximum concurrency limit (10); channel-level and workload-type concurrency cannot both be active for the same channel; every workload type assigned to contacts that route to this profile must have a corresponding row, or those contacts queue indefinitely.

metrics.name: Queue
metrics.summary: A queue that agents with this routing profile handle. You can add multiple queues to a routing profile.
metrics.description:
Use the dropdown menu or text field to choose a queue that you've already set up. You can add multiple queues to a routing profile. If you want a queue to handle several channels with a different priority per channel, add the queue once per channel.

In the **Manual assignment** section, queue and channel combinations are listed for routing with manual assignment, which supports tasks, emails, and chats.

metrics.name: Channels
metrics.summary: Whether this queue entry is for chat, voice, email, task, or all of them.
metrics.description:
Choose whether the queue is for chat, voice, email, task, or all of them.

**Important:** the channel that you specify here must also be enabled in the **Channel settings** section. If it isn't, contacts from that channel won't be routed to agents.

metrics.name: Priority
metrics.summary: The order in which contacts are to be handled for that queue; priority 1 is handled before priority 2.
metrics.description:
Specify the order in which contacts are to be handled for that queue. For example, a contact in a queue with a priority of 2 would be a lower priority than a contact in a queue with a priority of 1.

Priority takes precedence over delay. Priority for queues is relevant to searching for queues for an individual agent; it does not determine which agent out of multiple available agents is routed a contact. When priority and delay are equal, the oldest contact is routed first.

Valid values: 1 to 99.

metrics.name: Delay (in seconds)
metrics.summary: The minimum time a contact should be in the queue before it is routed to an available agent with this profile.
metrics.description:
Enter the minimum amount of time a contact should be in the queue before they are routed to an available agent.

The **Delay** setting means that X seconds must pass before this contact can be offered to agents with this routing profile; whether the agents are idle or not isn't taken into account. For example, with a 30-second delay a 15-second-old contact is not offered to an idle agent until it is at least 30 seconds old. When a delayed contact ages past its delay it is treated with the queue's priority alongside the other queues.

Valid values: 0 to 9999.

metrics.name: Schedule
metrics.summary: A generated set of agent shifts for a forecast group over a date range; a draft until published.
metrics.description: Connect generates the least number of shifts for agents based on the forecasted demand pattern and configured constraints to hit the optimization goal. After you create shift activities, shift profiles, staffing groups and staffing group rules, choose **Generate new** in Schedule manager. The result is a draft that agents and supervisors cannot see until you publish it; you can edit shifts, regenerate, search and sort schedules here.

metrics.name: Schedule type
metrics.summary: Schedule (a standard schedule) or Shift bid (a schedule agents bid on).
metrics.description:
+ **Schedule**: a standard schedule that is not a shift bid.
+ **Shift bid**: a schedule that agents bid on; see Shift bidding for how to set up and run a bid.

metrics.name: Schedule status
metrics.summary: In progress while generating, then Complete or Failed; publishing then makes it visible to agents.
metrics.description: A newly generated schedule shows **In progress**; generation takes 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on the number of agents, rules and the schedule duration. It then becomes **Complete** or **Failed**. Review warnings (HIGH: an agent was not scheduled; MEDIUM: scheduled but not all requirements met; LOW: minor issues such as overstaffing) and choose **Publish** when satisfied; a published schedule is visible to staff and supervisors in the staffing groups.

metrics.name: Bid status
metrics.summary: For Shift bid schedules, where the bidding process stands.
metrics.description: Applies to schedules of type **Shift bid**: it tracks the bidding round in which agents choose shifts before the schedule is finalised. Standard schedules show no bid status. See Shift bidding in the admin guide for the bid lifecycle.

metrics.name: Assignment method
metrics.summary: For Shift bid schedules, how bids are turned into assigned shifts.
metrics.description: Applies to **Shift bid** schedules: the method used to assign shifts from agents' bids once bidding closes. Standard schedules are assigned directly by the generator. See Shift bidding in the admin guide.

metrics.name: Schedule start and end dates
metrics.summary: The period the schedule covers; up to 18 weeks ahead.
metrics.description: The duration of the schedule. You can schedule up to 18 weeks out, within the published short-term forecast for the forecast group.

metrics.name: Forecast group
metrics.summary: The forecast group whose published short-term forecast the schedule or configuration is for.
metrics.description: The forecast group selected as schedule input. A schedule covers one forecast group (you cannot schedule for multiple groups at once), and its demand pattern drives how many agents are needed per interval. Staffing groups and trade groups are associated with a forecast group too.

metrics.name: Created
metrics.summary: When the item was created.
metrics.description: The date the schedule, activity, profile or group was created. Schedules can be sorted by creation date in Schedule manager.

metrics.name: Last published
metrics.summary: When the schedule was last published to agents and supervisors.
metrics.description: When you choose **Publish** and confirm, the schedule becomes official and visible to staff and supervisors in the staffing groups. This is the date of the most recent publish.

metrics.name: Last updated and updated by
metrics.summary: When the item was last changed and which user changed it.
metrics.description: The most recent update to the item and the user who made it. For schedules this includes edits to shifts and activities made before or after publishing.

metrics.name: Shift activity
metrics.summary: A block of time within a shift, such as Work, Break, Lunch, Training, PTO or Overtime.
metrics.description: Shift activities are the building blocks of a shift. Work activities are when agents handle contacts; others (Break, Lunch, Training, Overtime, PTO) are placed by the scheduler according to shift profiles or added to draft and published schedules as **Shared** (one occurrence for all selected agents) or **Individual** activities, with placement left as specified or optimised within the shift or a time window.

metrics.name: Activity type and sub-type
metrics.summary: Whether the activity is productive work or a non-work activity, and its category.
metrics.description: The type classifies the activity (for example Work versus non-productive activities such as Break, Lunch, Training, Time off or Overtime) and the sub-type refines it. Scheduling uses the type to know when agents are available for contacts and how the activity counts for adherence and pay.

metrics.name: Staff requestable
metrics.summary: Whether agents can request this activity themselves, for example time off or overtime.
metrics.description: Whether staff can request this activity from the agent workspace. Time-off and overtime style activities can be made requestable so agents choose when to take time off or work overtime within the parameters you set, without manual manager approval; eligibility is set per agent in Staff rules.

metrics.name: Duration
metrics.summary: How long the activity, or the rotation pattern, lasts.
metrics.description: For an activity, the length of time it occupies within a shift. For a shift rotation pattern, the number of weeks the pattern runs before it repeats.

metrics.name: Adherence
metrics.summary: Whether time in this activity is measured for schedule adherence.
metrics.description: Whether agents' real-time status is compared against this activity for schedule adherence. Adherence metrics (Adherent time, Non-adherent time, Adherence) are tracked for scheduled activities that count toward adherence.

metrics.name: Paid
metrics.summary: Whether time in this activity counts as paid hours.
metrics.description: Whether the activity is paid time. Paid hours feed the paid-hours variance used when agents trade shifts and the hours tracked against staff contract rules.

metrics.name: Shift profile
metrics.summary: A template of shift rules: start-time windows, shift length, days, and where activities such as breaks and lunch go.
metrics.description: A shift profile defines the shifts the generator may build: the activities and rules that apply, such as earliest and latest start, shift length, working days and break placement. Profiles are assigned to staffing groups, and an agent-level profile set in **Staff rules** overrides the group's profile.

metrics.name: Activities and rules
metrics.summary: The activities a profile schedules and the rules that constrain them.
metrics.description: The shift activities included in the profile (for example Work, Break, Lunch) and the rules that place them, such as how long after shift start a break may occur. The count summarises how many are configured.

metrics.name: Shift rotation pattern
metrics.summary: A multi-week sequence of shift profiles that agents rotate through.
metrics.description: A shift rotation pattern assigns a different shift profile to each step of a multi-week cycle, for example mornings one week and afternoons the next. Assign a pattern to agents in Staff rules (mutually exclusive with a single shift profile) and choose the step each agent starts on; the Generate schedule page shows the patterns in use for the forecast group.

metrics.name: Steps
metrics.summary: The ordered steps of the rotation, each pointing at a shift profile.
metrics.description: The number of steps in the rotation pattern. Each step is one period of the cycle and names the shift profile used during it; agents can start the rotation on any step.

metrics.name: Description
metrics.summary: Optional text describing the item.
metrics.description: Optional descriptive text entered when the item was created.

metrics.name: Staffing group
metrics.summary: The group of agents, with their supervisors, that a schedule is generated for.
metrics.description: Every agent must be in a staffing group for a schedule to be generated for them. A staffing group is associated with a forecast group and a shift profile, and lists the supervisors who can view its published schedules. A user cannot be an agent in one staffing group and a supervisor in another. Removing an agent does not delete their shifts, so remove the shifts first if they will not join another group.

metrics.name: Status
metrics.summary: Whether the item is active.
metrics.description: Whether the configuration item is active and used by scheduling, or inactive.

metrics.name: Approval type
metrics.summary: Whether shift trades in this trade group need manager approval or are approved automatically within the group's rules.
metrics.description: How trades between agents in the group are approved: automatically when they fall within the group's variance and notice rules, or by a supervisor. Agents must be marked eligible to trade shifts in Staff rules.

metrics.name: Notice period
metrics.summary: How far in advance of the shift a trade must be requested.
metrics.description: The minimum lead time before a shift starts for a trade request to be allowed in this trade group.

metrics.name: Trade and paid hours variance (minutes)
metrics.summary: How much the traded shifts may differ in duration and in paid hours.
metrics.description: The maximum difference, in minutes, allowed between the two shifts in a trade: **Trade duration variance** for shift length and **Paid hours variance** for paid time. Trades outside these limits are not allowed, or need approval depending on the approval type.
